mio: mio — my (unstressed possessive; mio Çid 'my lord Cid')
çid: Çid — the Cid, 'lord' (Arabic sīdī 'my lord'; pronounced Tsid)
sos: so — his, her, their (= modern sus)
avie: aver — he had (imperfect; unaccented spelling beside avié)
campeador: Campeador — the Battler, the Champion (the Cid's epithet, from campo 'field of battle')
fabló: fablar — he spoke (preterite; = habló, note f-)
ya: ya — O! (vocative particle, Arabic yā); also 'now, already'
al: a + el — to the; al menos 'even the least'
si: si — if; si + subjunctive alone = 'if only …!'
çinxo: çeñir — he girded (strong preterite 3rd sg.; Latin cinxit)
nada: nada — nothing; por nada 'for anything (in the world)'
burgos: Burgos — Burgos, chief city of Old Castile
averes: aver — goods, possessions, wealth (aver as noun, pl.)
las: el/la — the (fem. pl.); them (fem. object pronoun)
ha: aver — he has (3rd sg. present; = ha)
i: e/i — and (variant of e before some sounds)
tierra: tierra — land, country; one's own land
dixo: dezir — he/she said (strong preterite; x = sh-sound; = dijo)
commo: commo — as, like (spelling variant of como)
estávalos: estar + los — he-was + them: 'was … them' (estava + enclitic los)
ien: ien — they would (auxiliary of the split conditional: conbidar le ien = le convidarían; from avién)
cabo: cabo — beside, next to (preposition; cf. modern cabe)
diesse: dar — he should give (imperfect subjunctive; = diese)
